data.title: Python
data.tagline: A programming language often used to automate work on a computer or server
data.learningOutcome: You can identify where a Python script runs and which files it will read and write.
data.description: A Python script can read three Markdown notes and write their titles into `summary.csv`. It runs on a local machine or server; an ordinary web page does not execute a local Python script by itself.

learning.assumes: You know a folder can contain several files.
learning.outcome: You can identify where a Python script runs and which files it will read and write.

explanation.title: Choose the files
explanation.text: The script finds the `.md` files and reads their text.

explanation.title: Apply one rule
explanation.text: For example, it can use the first line of each note as a title.

explanation.title: Write the result
explanation.text: It creates `summary.csv` on the machine or server that ran it.

data.boundary: Before running a script, check its paths and whether it can overwrite files. A page button cannot directly run a script on your own computer.

lessonPractice.title: A Python script will summarize 200 Markdown files into CSV without overwriting sources. What preparation matters most before running?

options.label: Confirm input directory, output file, and overwrite rules, then test with a small copied sample
options.feedback: File automation risk comes from scope and writes, so explicit targets and a trial prevent batch damage.

options.label: Run it directly on all 200 production files and use editor Undo if the result is wrong
options.feedback: Batch scripts may write across files, and editor Undo may not cover the process; test scope and output on copies first.

options.label: Check only that the script starts, without verifying output columns, encoding, or malformed files
options.feedback: Starting proves only that syntax and runtime basically work, not that batch input, output, and error paths are safe.

data.agentPrompt: List the exact paths the Python script will read and write and overwrite no Markdown by default. Trial it on three copied files, show the resulting CSV and error report, and wait for confirmation before processing the full directory.
